extraction.name: Common Corpus: The Largest Collection of Ethical Data for LLM Pre-Training
extraction.description: Common Corpus is an open dataset for language model pre-training, containing about two trillion tokens of uncopyrighted or permissively licensed data. It includes multilingual data from diverse sources such as government, culture, science, code, web, and semantic data.
extraction.license: Various permissive licenses (e.g., Public Domain, CC-By, MIT, Apache-2.0)
extraction.creator: Pierre-Carl Langlais, Carlos Rosas Hinostroza, Mattia Nee, Catherine Amett, Pavel Chizhov, Eliot Krzystof Jones, Irène Girard, David Mach, Anastasia Stasenko, Ivan P. Yamshchikov
extraction.inLanguage: Multilingual (English, French, German, Spanish, Latin, Italian, Polish, Greek, Portuguese, Russian, etc.)
extraction.citeAs: Langlais, P.-C., Rosas Hinostroza, C., Nee, M., Amett, C., Chizhov, P., Jones, E. K., Girard, I., Mach, D., Stasenko, A., & Yamshchikov, I. P. (2025). Common Corpus: The Largest Collection of Ethical Data for LLM Pre-Training. arXiv:2506.01732.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected from various sources including government databases (SEC, WTO, AMF, TED, GATT), cultural heritage institutions (Gallica, Library of Congress, Europeana), open science repositories (OpenAlex, arXiv), code repositories (The Stack v1 and v2), web sources (Wikipedia, Wikisource, YouTube Commons, StackExchange), and semantic data (Wikidata).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Web API, Secondary Data analysis, Direct measurement, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data includes PDF documents, web pages, code files, audio transcripts, and RDF triples from sources like SEC EDGAR, WTO Documents Online, AMF, TED EU Tenders, GATT Library, Europarl, Caselaw Access Project, CourtListener, EUR-lex, Eurovoc, French open data, USPTO, UN Digital Library, OECD, Chronicle America, Europeana, Gallica, Biblioteca, OpenAlex, arXiv, The Stack, Wikipedia, Wikisource, YouTube Commons, StackExchange, and Wikidata.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Data spans from the 18th century to 2024, with specific collections covering periods such as 1690-1963 (US PD Newspapers), 1618-1990 (Europeana Newspapers), 1794-1957 (German PD Newspapers), 1737-1905 (German PD), 1841-1879 (BnL Newspapers), 1946-1996 (GATT Library), 1993-2024 (SEC), 1995-2024 (WTO), and 2019-2022 (USPTO).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For Open Code, files were filtered by file extensions, licenses, and quality filters (e.g., removing files with 75% or more digits). Sequences of [\r]+\n were replaced with \n.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Text segmentation using Segmentext, OCR error detection using OCRoscope and OCRerrcr, OCR correction using OCRonos, PII removal using Microsoft Presidio with custom regex patterns, toxicity detection using Celadon classifier, and license verification.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations include license information, language identification (using fastText), and document creation year. For Wikidata, items and properties were translated into natural language sequences.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Segmentext, OCRoscope, OCRerrcr, OCRonos, Microsoft Presidio, Celadon, fastText
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Common Corpus is an evolving resource with versioning on HuggingFace. Past versions are archived for reproducibility. The dataset is maintained by PleIAs.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Personally Identifiable Information (PII) such as phone numbers, email addresses, and IP addresses were identified and replaced with fictitious but realistic values.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to support open science and ethical AI development, enabling LLM training without copyright infringement. It has been used by European labs and industry leaders like Anthropic.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Historical texts may contain harmful language reflecting outdated cultural norms. Toxicity filtering was applied to mitigate biases related to race, gender, religion, ability, and violence.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset does not cover all available open data (open data paradox). Coverage for low-resource languages is shallow. The 2 trillion tokens are suitable for small to medium models but not for very large models. The dataset is not directly suitable for instruction-tuning or task-specific fine-tuning.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Pre-training of large language models, training of multimodal models, classifiers, synthetic datasets, benchmarks, and retrieval augmented generation (RAG) models.
